research_question: How do the three existing role-configured agents (analyst, extractor, synthesist) perform on authentic software issue reports when each independently receives the same frozen issue packet and bounded official context?

task_source_policy.prior_public_disclosure_policy: Freeze the issue report and attached official context; audit comments/fixes separately. Publicly disclosed tasks remain leakage-flagged exploratory cases and are never represented as blind discovery.

agent_protocol.seed_policy: Reuse the existing run's per-request SHA-256 seed scheme with distinct seeds per task, role and repetition; record the seed in run metadata. Keep the configured worker temperature at 0.0 and max output at 512 tokens, so repetitions are repeat-request consistency checks under the fixed decoding configuration rather than deliberate sampling diversity.
agent_protocol.comparison_policy: Use the existing analyst, extractor and synthesist model-plus-system-prompt configurations from llm_poc_rewrite; run each independently on the exact same issue packet, not as an orchestrated pipeline. Limit each agent-task-repetition trace to one API request; the total per-task budget equals the three configured agent requests. Report role/model/prompt bundles descriptively per issue; do not attribute differences to model identity alone, agent frameworks or allocation strategy. Public-exposure leakage is an explicit limitation.

evaluation.blinding: Remove model, issue number and repetition identifiers; randomize final-response order and use unrelated blind IDs. Raters see the frozen issue brief and context, not comments, known fixes, disclosure notes or model identity. A separate custodian retains the blind mapping.
evaluation.rating_scale: Each dimension is scored 0-4: 0 absent or wrong; 1 mostly unsupported; 2 partially useful with material gaps; 3 sound and actionable; 4 precise, complete, and well-calibrated.

claim_limits: This is a text-only authentic issue task transfer pilot, not a patch-generation or code-correctness benchmark.
No repository clone, code execution, patch application, test execution, or framework comparison is performed.
Results describe three fixed role/model/prompt bundles on two issue families; they do not establish broad production coding ability or model superiority.
Public fixes and comments can leak answers; report the recorded leakage classification and do not interpret these cases as blind discovery.
The selected issues #10694 and #10477 represent distinct technical families, but both are public historical reports with comment-derived hints.
The three tested units are existing role/model/prompt bundles; any score difference is confounded by both model identity and the role-specific system prompt.
The two issue tasks × three configured agents × three repetitions produce 18 responses and 36 human ratings at two raters per response.
Only issue reports and bounded attached documentation context are provided; the model has no browser or repository tools.
